title: Collections Desk Guide: First-Delinquency Relief on Retail Installment Contract Late Charges
content:
**Rule.** A first-delinquency reduction applies to a late charge on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts according to the late charges assessed on the contract, waived or not, in the rolling 12 months ending on the assessment date:

- with **none**, the first-delinquency reduction is **50 percent**;
- with **exactly one**, it is **25 percent**;
- with **two or more**, there is no first-delinquency reduction.

**What is counted.** Every late charge assessed on the same contract and dated in the rolling 12 months ending on the assessment date, whatever installment it was charged on, and whether or not it was later waived. The rolling 12 months run from records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the assessment date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) through the assessment date. Fees of other kinds are not counted.

| Late charges assessed in the rolling 12 months | First-delinquency reduction |
|---|---|
| 0 | 50 percent |
| 1 | 25 percent |
| 2 | none |
| 3 or more | none |

**Points of judgement (hypothetical histories, assessment on 14 October).**

- One late charge dated 15 October of the previous year, and none since: that charge is dated later than 14 October of the previous year, so it is inside the window and the reduction is 25 percent.
- One late charge dated 14 October of the previous year, and none since: it is not later than the same calendar day 12 months before, so the count is 0 and the reduction is 50 percent.
- Two late charges in the window, one of them waived as a courtesy: both count, so there is no first-delinquency reduction.
